author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Nashua Community College is launching a new group of community education and enrichment courses this fall, opening college-led instruction to local teenagers and adults outside its degree programs. The schedule mixes practical skills, creative work, wellness and recreation in formats ranging from single sessions to multiweek classes.

A basic vehicle-maintenance class for new drivers is scheduled for October 10 and is open to participants age 15 and older. The hands-on session is designed to cover tire pressure, dashboard warning lights, fluid checks, jump-starting a vehicle, changing a tire and basic inspections.

An eight-week creative-writing workshop begins September 16, with instruction in memoir, personal essays and fiction. Other listed options include yoga, a healthy-lunchbox workshop, tabletop role-playing games, pumpkin-cake decorating, comfort cooking and an Italian-cookie class.

Prices and age requirements vary by course, and the college says additional offerings will be announced. The initiative broadens the school’s role as a community training hub by pairing short, accessible classes with instructors from the college and the region. Registration information is available through Nashua Community College’s non-credit course page.
dek: The fall lineup includes vehicle maintenance, creative writing, cooking, yoga and tabletop games, with courses ranging from one session to eight weeks.
headline: Nashua Community College opens new enrichment classes to teens and adults
